A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLIP research. All 22 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning, video-generation and policy experiments in Section 5, plus real-robot results, ablations and robustness analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the planning success rates in Table 1 and real-robot evaluations in Table 8.

M1.justification: The CVAE flow generator, flow-conditioned video diffusion model, clip-based LIV fine-tuning, planning algorithm and low-level policies remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same LIBERO, FMB, Bridge-V2, Language-Table and other manipulation scenarios. The real-robot tasks and visual-distraction scenarios in Appendix B are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including UniPi, LVDM, IRASim, ATM, diffusion policy, OpenVLA and the FLIP variants. The appendix comparisons were already present in v1.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix B retain the same training and testing sample counts, image resolutions, human assessment procedure, evaluation metrics and robot testing protocols. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The module ablations, policy-conditioning comparisons, model and data scaling analyses, and visual-distraction failure studies are retained unchanged, including Appendices B.3, B.5 and B.6.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the error bars in Figures 5 and 12 and the discussion of policy variance. No seed information, repeated-run counts or statistical tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings match across versions. For example, FLIP's LIBERO-LONG planning success remains 100% in Table 1, and its real-robot success rates remain 55% for tea scooping and 50% for cloth unfolding in Table 8.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, planning objective and Bellman reasoning, diffusion equations, and LIV losses in Appendix A are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about planning, video generation, policy guidance and scalability. The revised title emphasizes the world-model framing already explicit in v1.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including slow planning and restriction to quasi-static tasks, missing physical and 3D information, and the appendix discussion of susceptibility to visual distractions.

D1.justification: The policy implementation details in Appendix A.3, hyperparameters in Tables 5–6, robot hardware and control settings in Appendix B.4, and disclosed website information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and relationships to prior research. The title and publication-header updates do not introduce a new novelty claim or substantive research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'for General-Purpose Manipulation Tasks' to 'as General-Purpose Manipulation World Model', and the header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'. Body wording and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Spacing and page breaks change: Figure 3 moves upward, and the conclusion fits entirely on page 10 instead of continuing onto page 11. Figures and tables retain their content and basic design; appendix pages are visually identical below the updated headers.

improvement.justification: v2 updates the title and publication formatting while preserving the scientific argument, methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and limitations, including all appendix analyses. These limited editorial and layout changes establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
